QUOTE: "So this is a naming guard, not an access control. C has no member visibility, and the spelling is the only thing standing between a user and the field. ... The field is still there under the mangled name ... It does not change the struct layout, so the ABI is the same either way."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says opacity is enforced at compile time by renaming the member (`private_##member`), with the field still present and the layout unchanged.
